question: A 40-year-old male visits a urologist and reports that for the past 2 weeks, his penis has been gradually curving to the right with associated pain during intercourse. He is able to have a normal erection and he does not recollect of any trauma to his penis. Although he is married, he admits to having unprotected sexual relationship with several females in the past year. His vitals are normal and physical examination in unremarkable except for a lesionless curved penis. It is painless to touch. Test results for sexually transmitted disease is pending. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Unprotected sexual relationships with multiple partners -> increased risk of sexually transmitted diseases -> possible syphilis infection -> 70% CHAIN: Gradual penile curvature with pain during intercourse -> possible Peyronie's disease -> 60% CHAIN: Painless curved penis with no trauma history -> possible fibrosis of tunica albuginea -> 50% CHAIN: Lesionless curved penis -> less likely syphilitic chancre -> 40% CHAIN: Normal erection despite penile curvature -> less likely hypertrophy of corpus cavernosa -> 70%
analysis: Given the gradual onset of penile curvature with associated pain during intercourse in a sexually active individual, along with the absence of trauma and pending STD test results, the most likely cause is Peyronie's disease, which is characterized by fibrosis of the tunica albuginea.
